note.title: Reflexives and negatives
note.overview: This lesson contains 62 enabled questions. It teaches Reflexives and negatives through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Reflexives and negatives.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Feminine/plural agreement is required where shown.
Body-part phrases such as brossé les dents normally keep brossé.
In perfect negatives, put pas/jamais/rien/plus around the auxiliary.
Keep the reflexive pronoun inside the negative frame.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: je me réveille
workedExamples.why: Source pair: je me réveille → je me suis réveillé(e). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: je me lève
workedExamples.why: Source pair: je me lève → je me suis levé(e). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: je me lave
workedExamples.why: Source pair: je me lave → je me suis lavé(e). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: je me comporte bien / mal
workedExamples.answer: je me suis bien / mal comporté(e)
workedExamples.why: Source pair: je me comporte bien / mal → je me suis bien / mal comporté(e). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: je m’ennuie
workedExamples.why: Source pair: je m’ennuie → je me suis ennuyé(e). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

commonMistakes: Putting the negative after the participle.
Adding agreement to brossé les dents in the taught body-part example.
A small article or ending can change the grammar even when the main vocabulary is recognisable.
Do not change a correct answer into an error just because the learner also wrote the subject.
Do not use avoir or drop me/se.
detailedExplanation: This lesson contains 62 enabled questions. It teaches Reflexives and negatives through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.

Build the sentence around the conjugated verb, place the negative accurately and recheck articles after the negative. A small article, auxiliary or agreement error can change the grammar even when the main vocabulary is recognisable.
examTips: Underline every task requirement before writing and tick each one after it is included.
Build the verb and tense core first; then check articles, negatives and agreement.
